findings.statement: A lane that has no ShellCheck 0.11.0 on PATH and no network cannot run the gate: curl at shellcheck.sh:28 fails (exit 22, 403) with a bare curl error that does not name the gate, so the playbook step in opening-a-pr.md:9 cannot be followed.

The download path and the pinned Linux checksum have not been tested at rung 4 on any machine; only the PR's fixture CI job will exercise them, and a wrong digest would turn every project's first CI step red.
Any uname pair other than Linux.x86_64 or Darwin.arm64 (for example Linux aarch64 / ubuntu-24.04-arm, or Intel macOS) exits 1 with 'not pinned' unless 0.11.0 is already on PATH.
An executable already cached under ${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/shellcheck-0.11.0 is reused and exec'd without a checksum, so a binary planted there runs (shown with a planted script).
Checked whether tar -xJf needs an xz binary: macOS bsdtar has liblzma and Ubuntu ships xz.
Checked sha256sum against shasum: both are present, and both accept the same check line.

A project that edited its ci.yml goes through git merge-file during update (the clone has no tags, so there is no base). It ends up with ci.yml.factory-merge, no gate step in its live ci.yml, and nothing in the doctor reports it.
The fixture job's new step runs the zero-argument gate inside an applied project; tested on a project built from the template, it checks 11 files and exits 0.
cmd_apply copies template/.github/shellcheck.sh with cp -p (factory918.sh:137), so the file stays mode 755.
The factory-root symlink .github/shellcheck.sh is tracked as mode 120000 with a relative target; checkout restores it and sync leaves git status clean.
Removing the bash -n step loses nothing: ShellCheck rejects syntax errors such as a missing fi with error-level findings (SC1046/SC1072 etc.) and exits 1.
In a project that deleted its hooks, the zero-argument form checks only the gate itself (files checked: 1) and passes, even though the script promises a refusal in that case.
The source-path=SCRIPTDIR directives in the spec-review tests let a per-file shellcheck -x run from another directory pass; without them the files give SC1091/SC2154.
The set -f claim in delegation.sh's directive reasons holds: line 7 is set -fuo pipefail and nothing turns it off.
The delegation.sh hook (and the other shipped scripts the diff touches) changed only in comment lines; the code with comments stripped is identical, and 55 hook assertions pass.
The cmd_sync edits are equivalent: ${skills:?} can never fire because skills is derived from TEMPLATE, the array count matches the old ls|wc count (72), and sync leaves git status clean.
The new doctor shellcheck line is only ever PASS or NOTE and sits above 'slots filled', so factory-start day zero and factory-doctor's table are unaffected; the models-sheet output is unchanged.
The cross-cutting predicate at review-brief.sh:189 does not match .github/shellcheck.sh or the workflows, so later edits to the gate get no blast-radius brief.
While a review is in progress, the hook still reads .claude/state/review unchanged, and its Bash scanner never blocks running the gate.
The vendored, unpatched show-me-your-work log.sh and worktree-audit.sh are now linted. They pass today, but an upstream bump that introduces a finding would need a new patch.
wizard/template.sh is outside every gate glob yet has a real SC2034 at line 19, so widening the glob would turn CI red, and a lane that edits it fails a gate that CI never runs.
wizard/SKILL.md:41 still tells readers to run bash -n.
The file-level SC2016 directive at review-brief.sh:17 would also hide any future genuine SC2016 in that file.
At the factory root, the zero-argument form checks only 6 of the 20 files and still passes, giving a misleading green result.
Check 6 in tests/shellcheck/gate.sh hardcodes PATH with /usr/bin and assumes no ShellCheck 0.11.0 there; a runner image that ships 0.11.0 would make the test fail.
After update, an existing project whose hooks were edited (and so kept) or that has its own scripts is linted by the new first CI step and can go red.
The doctor prints PASS for any ShellCheck version (for example apt's 0.10.0), even though the gate will ignore that copy and download the pin.
The doctor's shellcheck NOTE says the gate will download the tool and that its absence blocks nothing, which is false in an offline sandbox.
The fixture's apply step pipes through tail -30, and the extra doctor line pushes one more line out of the visible log; this affects display only.
update writes the gate with mode 0644, which is harmless because every documented call starts with bash.
The knowledge build and check stay clean, and P25 is generated into template/docs/factory918/DECISIONS.md.
The fake-gh.sh:15 rewrite from an && || chain to an if keeps the same two branches.
The line shifts in delegation.sh break no delegation.sh:<n> citation, because none exist outside research/.
The gate and the CLI changes run correctly under macOS's bash 3.2.
Checked for SIGPIPE misfires in the version check at shellcheck.sh:18; 0 of 300 runs misfired.
